title: Giving & receiving feedback
examples: How can I make my feedback sound less critical?
What is the difference between criticism and constructive feedback?
Can you give me an example of the SBI model in a meeting?

explain.say: Today we are learning a useful way to give and receive feedback.
The first part of the model is Situation; you name when it happened.
Next is Behavior; you describe what was seen or heard.
Finally, Impact; you explain the result of that behavior.
For a real-life example, imagine a team presentation went poorly.

items: Last Tuesday's review | You missed the deadline | The client seemed worried

explain.say: A common mistake is making the feedback too judgmental or vague.

faq.q: How do I start giving feedback if I feel awkward?
faq.a: Start by stating your intention to help the person improve. You can also say, "I wanted to share some thoughts on..." or "Can we talk about..."?
asks: How do I bring up difficult topics?
What is a good opening line for feedback?

faq.q: What if the person gets defensive when I give feedback?
faq.a: Stay calm and remember to focus only on the specific behavior, not the person. You can try saying, "I understand this is hard to hear." or "Let's focus on the task itself."?
asks: What if they argue with me?

faq.q: Is the SBI model only for negative feedback?
faq.a: No, it works for positive feedback too. You can say, "In that meeting, when you summarized the data, the impact was that everyone understood the next steps." or "Remember to use SBI for praise."?
asks: Can I use SBI for compliments?
Does SBI only work for problems?

faq.q: What is the difference between feedback and criticism?
faq.a: Feedback is about specific actions and future improvement, while criticism can sound like a personal attack. You can rephrase it by focusing on the action, not the character. You might ask, "Is this feedback or criticism?"?
asks: How do I avoid sounding critical?

faq.q: Should I give feedback immediately or wait?
faq.a: For minor issues, immediate feedback is best while details are fresh. For major issues, it is better to schedule a private time to discuss it. You can ask, "Is now a good time to chat?"?
asks: When is the best time to talk?
Should I wait until the review meeting?

facts: The SBI model stands for Situation, Behavior, and Impact.
Feedback should always be specific, focusing on observable actions.
When receiving feedback, it is helpful to listen without interrupting.
Giving feedback is a skill that improves with practice.

quiz.say: A colleague consistently arrives late to the morning stand-up meeting. Which statement correctly uses the SBI model?
quiz.show: Situation: Yesterday's meeting. Behavior: You arrived fifteen minutes late. Impact: We had to delay the whole agenda.

options.show: Situation: Yesterday's meeting. Behavior: You arrived fifteen minutes late. Impa
options.say: Situation: Yesterday's meeting. Behavior: You arrived fifteen minutes late. Impa

options.show: You are always late, which makes the team look unprofessional.
options.say: You are always late, which makes the team look unprofessional.

options.show: The meeting was delayed because of your tardiness.
options.say: The meeting was delayed because of your tardiness.

options.show: You need to be on time for all meetings.
options.say: You need to be on time for all meetings.

quiz.why: This option clearly names the time, describes the action, and explains the consequence.

wrong.1: This is judgmental and uses generalizations instead of specific facts.
wrong.2: This misses the crucial step of describing the specific behavior observed.
wrong.3: This is too vague and does not pinpoint a specific situation or impact.

quiz.say: When receiving feedback, what is the best initial response?

options.show: Thank the person for taking the time to share their thoughts.
options.say: Thank the person for taking the time to share their thoughts.

options.show: Immediately explain why the feedback is incorrect.
options.say: Immediately explain why the feedback is incorrect.

options.show: Wait until you have all the facts before responding.
options.say: Wait until you have all the facts before responding.

options.show: Ask the person to provide more examples right away.
options.say: Ask the person to provide more examples right away.

quiz.why: Acknowledging the effort shows professionalism, even if you disagree with the feedback.

wrong.1: This becomes defensive and shuts down the conversation before understanding the point.
wrong.2: While thinking is good, initial acknowledgement is needed to validate the speaker.
wrong.3: This can sound confrontational and pressures the giver to perform immediately.
